failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase: it is noted on the nightly card, becomes a draft once its count how often it fires, and is registered when you say yes. It is then tested on 2000-2023 only at a the strict pass mark, then runs as a paper trial on live sessions (20 recorded). It is admitted only if it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the leak check and you say yes. Even then, only an admitted idea may use the allocated paper capital, and no rule has reached that step yet.

problems.why: It leans on unexplained internal terms like 'staircase', 'nightly card', 'leak check' and 'admitted', and the 'strict pass mark' step is never explained, so a beginner would not follow the pipeline.

The garbled phrases 'becomes a draft once its count how often it fires' and 'at a the strict pass mark' make the stages unclear, so the answer does not clearly explain how an idea moves from draft to allocated paper capital.
